studies.name: Hunt X, Saran A, White H, Kuper H. Effectiveness of interventions for improving educational outcomes for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2025;21:e70016.
studies.draft_uses: Full published review (February 6, 2025); all substantive claims in the draft draw on this version — 18 studies in skills-for-learning analysis, 12 with significant effects, 28 studies total, low confidence ratings, twin-track framing, calls for systemic approaches.
studies.latest_known: Same publication, February 6, 2025 (Campbell Systematic Reviews, 21, e70016). No corrigendum, update, or superseding review found as of November 2026. Search note: the review's own literature search was closed March 2022; the review was accepted October 2024 and published February 2025. No newer version identified.
studies.what_changed: N/A — no superseding readout found. Figures cited in the draft (12/18 significant effects on skills for learning, low confidence ratings, 28 included studies, twin-track recommendation) are consistent with the published February 2025 version.

studies.name: Saran A, White H, Kuper H. Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low-and middle-income countries. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2020;16(1):e1070.
studies.draft_uses: 2020 original EGM: claims that over half of impact evaluations come from upper-middle-income countries, notable gap for low-income countries (n=9), significant gap in study quality especially for impact evaluations, focus of studies on 'fixing individuals', calls for more studies from low-income countries and on all impairment types.
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (e1104, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1104) was published July 12, 2020, correcting errors in the original January 2020 EGM. The draft explicitly states it found this correction but could not hold it, and declares that nothing in the draft draws on this source — yet the draft does in fact cite and quote specific figures from [2] (e.g., 'over half of the impact evaluations in that map come from upper-middle-income countries, with notable gaps for low-income countries (n = 9)'). A separate but related UNICEF Innocenti 'Inclusion Matters 2024' EGM (published April 2025) updates the evidence landscape for inclusive interventions for children with disabilities in LMICs, but is a distinct product with a different scope and does not formally supersede the Saran 2020 Campbell EGM. No updated Campbell EGM replacing Saran 2020 on the same topic was found.
studies.what_changed: A published corrigendum (July 12, 2020) corrects errors in the original EGM. The draft states it cannot access this correction and therefore draws nothing from [2], but in practice the draft does cite specific figures from [2] — including the upper-middle-income country share of impact evaluations and the low-income country count (n=9) — without being able to verify whether those figures were among those corrected. The specific figures the draft quotes from [2] cannot be confirmed as post-correction values. Additionally, the UNICEF 'Inclusion Matters 2024' update (April 2025) represents a broader, more recent mapping of the same evidence space, though it is not a direct replacement of the Campbell EGM.

studies.name: Ahmed SK, Jeffries D, Chakraborty A, et al. Teacher professional development for disability inclusion in low- and middle-income Asia-Pacific countries: An evidence and gap map. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2022;18(4):e1287.
studies.draft_uses: 2022 EGM: 50 studies found across 16 of 41 countries; focus on changing teacher attitudes; qualitative reports of teacher-reported benefits (e.g., Vietnam seminars); only three studies on mental health support for students with disability; no interventions supporting students during emergencies; no studies on supporting positive student behaviour; call for more published evidence from disability-inclusive TPD interventions in LMICs.
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (e1315, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1315, PMID: 36913230) was published February 25, 2023, correcting errors in the original November 2022 EGM. The draft explicitly states it found this correction but could not read it, and declares that nothing in the draft draws on [3] — yet the draft does in fact cite and quote specific figures and findings from [3] throughout (e.g., '50 studies', '16 of 41 countries', 'only three studies on mental health', 'none support students during emergencies', 'no studies on positive student behaviour'). No full updated version of this EGM replacing the 2022 publication was found.
studies.what_changed: A published corrigendum (February 25, 2023) corrects errors in the original EGM. The draft states it cannot access this correction and therefore draws nothing from [3], but in practice the draft cites specific figures from [3] — including the count of 50 studies, the 16-of-41-countries figure, the three-studies-on-mental-health figure, and the finding that no interventions support students during emergencies — without being able to verify whether any of those figures were among those corrected. The specific figures the draft quotes from [3] cannot be confirmed as post-correction values.
